supple

SUP-ul · adjective

What It Means

Supple is bending and moving easily and gracefully, flexible in a smooth, natural way rather than a stiff one.

The gymnast's supple limbs folded into the pretzel-like pose without a single strained muscle.

Example

After months of stretching, his once-stiff hamstrings became supple enough to touch his toes flat-palmed.

Supple can describe a flexible body, but also flexible materials -- supple leather, for example, bends easily instead of cracking.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

flexible: Flexible means able to bend easily without breaking -- a flexible ruler, a flexible wire -- and it says nothing about how the bending looks. Supple adds grace and ease: a supple body or material does not merely tolerate bending, it bends smoothly, as if bending were natural to it.

lithe: Lithe describes a whole body that is thin, supple, and graceful in motion, like a cat or a dancer -- it always paints a slim, agile figure. Supple is broader: it can describe a single joint, a muscle, or a strip of leather, and it points at the easy bending itself.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

rigid: unable to bend; stiff

stiff: not easily bent; inflexible

Where it sits · how graceful the bending is — pliable → supple → lissome

pliable vs. supple: Pliable describes a more basic kind of easy bending or shaping, without supple's added sense of gracefulness.

lissome vs. supple: Lissome goes a step beyond supple -- an almost effortless, whole-body gracefulness, the kind used of a dancer, while supple can describe one knee, one wrist, or one well-worn glove.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — sup-

prefix — sup-: under (the form Latin sub- takes before a p)

root — ple

root — ple: to fold, to bend (from Latin plicare, 'to fold')

Put it together

Put it together: Supple is built from sup- ('under' -- the form Latin sub- takes before a p) + ple ('to fold, to bend,' from Latin plicare). Latin supplex originally meant 'kneeling, bending under,' describing something that bends or folds easily, whether a body or a material.
